title: Trump’s Special Envoy Hauled In More Than $250 Million While in Government
partialText: A disclosure shows that Steve Witkoff collected nearly $107 million in 2025 from a holding company that includes a crypto business owned by his family and President Trump’s.

title: Trump Announces $500 Rebates for Some Obamacare Customers, Weeks Before the Election
partialText: The White House plans to send the money to people in 30 states who have higher incomes and are insured under the Affordable Care Act.

title: Jimmy Kimmel Moves Talarico Interview to YouTube Because of F.C.C. ‘Threat’
partialText: In a monologue on Wednesday, Mr. Kimmel said that the show made the decision because the F.C.C. had “threatened” ABC over “traditional editorial decisions.”

title: The U.S. Open Has Been Quietly Releasing Tickets for Its Popular Tournament
partialText: On Wednesday, hundreds appeared on Ticketmaster. The United States Tennis Association said it periodically released tickets it held for a variety of reasons.

title: Trump’s Trade War With Canada Is Making Even Sprinkle Makers Nervous
partialText: President Trump’s levies on a long, eclectic list of products from Canada have companies scrambling to figure out if their supply chains are affected.

title: A.I. Data Center Pollution Poses Health Threat, Former E.P.A. Officials Warn
partialText: Air pollution from gas-fired power plants to run data centers is expected to add at least $20 billion in annual health care costs by 2028, the group warns.

title: Oil Prices Surge as Stocks and Bonds Wobble
partialText: Crude oil hit its highest levels in months and bond yields continued to rise as investors worried about diminishing energy supplies and the prospect of accelerating inflation.

title: European Central Bank Raises Rates in Bid to Quell Inflation
partialText: The bank, fighting price pressures spurred by the war in the Middle East, raised its benchmark rate to 2.5 percent.

title: A $5,000 ‘Trump Dividend’? The Bond Market May Like a Word.
partialText: President Trump’s latest political gambit could cost more than $1 trillion, and further roil a volatile bond market.

title: Why November Is Becoming the Best Time for Off-Season Travel
partialText: The increasing popularity of September and October travel has changed the traditional shoulder season, leaving sporadic midweek troughs and a few weeks in November.

title: Voters Are Asking A.I. About Elections. The Answers Can Vary by User.
partialText: Artificial intelligence is quickly becoming a go-to stop for voters looking for information about political races. Researchers are studying the effects.

title: Help! We Canceled a Vacation Rental 2 Years Ago. Where’s Our $13,000?
partialText: In July 2024, a couple used Booking.com to reserve two apartments in Hawaii, but quickly changed their minds. Getting a refund was no day at the beach.

title: Eurail, the Longtime Savior of Shoestring Backpackers, Ditches Its Name

title: Justice Dept. Investigates Nvidia Deal With Groq

title: Joseph Rice, Lowcountry Lawyer Who Took On Big Tobacco, Dies at 72
partialText: He challenged tobacco companies as well as the opioid industry, securing multibillion-dollar settlements that also benefited public health.

title: Bond Market Rebuffs Treasury’s $6 Billion Plan to Reduce Borrowing Costs
partialText: The 10-year yield rose to its highest level in three years, suggesting investors were underwhelmed by the details of a move to buy back government bonds.

title: Saudi Oil Exports Plunge as Spread of War Shuts Off Shipping Routes
partialText: With few good options for safely shipping oil, Saudi Arabia’s exports have fallen to a 13-year low.

title: Why California Is Reconsidering Its Decision to Shun Nuclear Power

title: As He Backs ICE Crackdown, Nebraska Governor Employs Undocumented Workers

title: Politics News Site NOTUS Rebrands as The Washington Sun

title: TSA PreCheck Now Unlocks Access to Visit Airports Without a Plane Ticket
partialText: At more than a dozen U.S. airports, T.S.A. PreCheck members can now apply to enter the secure area, even if they’re just going to meet someone on a flight.

title: Roger Marshall Sued 700 Patients for Debts; 81 Were Arrested. Now He’s a Senator.
partialText: Patients sued by Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas were routinely charged 18 percent interest, The Times found. Some had bank accounts garnished.

title: Seaweed Is Their Way of Life. A Company’s Sweeping Plan Threatens It.

title: The C.E.O. Teaching Future Generations About 9/11
